title: Audit playbook scratch - Kim
content:
Context / purpose:
- Working scratch for SOC2 readiness runbook focused on evidence collection and control owners. Not for broad distribution.

High-level goals (what I want from this doc):
1) Capture a minimal evidence map per control family (IAM, Change Management, Logging, Incident Response, Vendor mgmt).
2) Surface open/incomplete artifacts that need owners and deadlines.
3) Quick checklist for pilots (hosted API + Dedicated infra + Private VPC).
4) Notes-to-self on where to pull logs/exports and short queries to use.

Scope / assumptions:
- In-scope services: Redwood API (hosted), Redwood Dedicated (reserved clusters), Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem package).
- Exclude: marketing cookies, personal accounts.
- Timebox for initial pass: 4 weeks to produce evidence packets for Type I style review.

Control family breakdown (rough):
1) Access Control (AC)
   - Owner: Ibrahim (SRE lead)
   - Evidence candidates: IAM role inventory export (aws iam list-roles CSV), GCP IAM policy snapshots, Okta group membership report, SSH bastion access logs, onboarding/offboarding checklist from HR sync.
   - TODO: script to export current Okta groups and map to repos/orgs (SEC-338).
   - Open questions: do we want to include ephemeral token rotation proof for service accounts? where to store rotation records?

2) Change Management (CM)
   - Owner: Maya (Platform eng PM)
   - Evidence: GitHub PR approvals, protected branch rules screenshot, deploy pipeline run IDs (CI job numbers), release notes, infra-as-code PR linking to ticket.
   - Quick notes: need a small dashboard showing PR->deploy lineage for 90-day window (query: GH API for merged PRs with label "deploy" + Circle/Buildkite run id).
   - Risk: small on-call fixes merged directly; need exemption process documented.

3) Logging & Monitoring (LM)
   - Owner: Kim (me) but SRE owns logs
   - Evidence: retained log export from central logging (last 90 days), alert history for critical alerts (PagerDuty/Opsgenie logs), sample alert runbook, metrics dashboard snapshots.
   - Action: confirm retention policies for hosted vs private customers. Where are private deployment logs kept (customer-managed)? note that for Private we only demonstrate control over the control plane.

4) Incident Response (IR)
   - Owner: SRE lead + Security on-call rotation
   - Evidence: incident postmortem examples (anonymized), runbook, tabletop exercises schedule, escalation matrix.
   - Gap: need at least one tabletop in past 12 months with notes — schedule Q1 run (owner: Omar).

5) Vendor and 3rd party management (VD)
   - Owner: Legal + Procurement (not sure who at our size)
   - Evidence: vendor inventory (SaaS list), data processing agreements, risk assessment notes.
   - TODO: get a current vendor list export from Airtable (Confluence link?), tag vendors that handle customer data.

Evidence matrix (very rough initial):
- AC-1 (user provisioning): Okta CSV + HR termination log + onboarding checklist (Confluence page id: CONF-142)
- CM-2 (change approvals): PR list with approvals (GH export) + protected branches screenshot
- LM-3 (retention): Logging export (ELK archive) + retention policy doc (confluence id)
- IR-1 (postmortems): 3 anonymized postmortems in last 12 months + tabletop notes

Notes-to-self on where to pull things (hacks):
- Okta: Admin console -> Reports -> Export groups (monthly). Use "reporting/okta-groups.sh" script in infra repo.
- AWS/GCP IAM: use terraform state to map role definitions; use aws cli inventory scripts under tools/iam-export.
- GitHub: use enterprise API to pull PRs and check protected-branch settings. Auth token stored in secrets manager (rotated).
- Logs: Kibana -> export query (time=90d), use s3 archival path s3://redwood-logs/archives/YYYY-MM.

Open/unknown items (needs owners):
- Private deployments: exact evidence we can show auditors for customer-managed infra (ask solutions-engineering).
- KMS/HSM integration: prove key lifecycle management for Private customers — legal/crypto team to provide notes.
- Automated proof of least-privilege for service accounts (still manual today).

Risks & mitigations (short):
- Risk: ad-hoc fixes bypassing PR -> weak change mgmt; Mitigation: enforce no direct pushes to main, enforce branch protections and emergency change log.
- Risk: missing log retention for private installs; Mitigation: require customers to sign standard BYO-logs agreement or provide a collector.

Meeting notes (2026-02-20 sync with SRE/Product):
- Ibrahim: will produce Okta group export by 2026-02-26.
- Maya: working on PR->deploy dashboard; target prototype by 2026-03-10.
- Omar: will schedule tabletop before end of March.
- Action: Kim to draft evidence packet template (this doc -> template) by 2026-02-28.

Evidence packet template (minimal fields):
- control_id | control_description | owner | artifact_type | artifact_location | date_range | extraction_steps | notes
- Example: AC-1 | user onboarding/offboarding | Ibrahim | CSV export | s3://evidence/AC-1-2026-02 | export command + filters | must redact PII before sharing

Quick checklist for next 2 weeks:
- [ ] Create evidence packet skeleton for AC + CM + LM (Kim) — due 2026-02-28
- [ ] Okta export + mapping to repos (Ibrahim) — due 2026-02-26
- [ ] Prototype PR->deploy extract (Maya) — due 2026-03-10
- [ ] Schedule tabletop (Omar) — due 2026-03-25

Draft wording for auditor cover email (notes):
"Attached is the evidence packet for control families X/Y/Z. All artifacts are either system exports or screenshots with extraction steps. Where artifacts contain PII, entries have been redacted and a redaction log is included."

Other freeform thoughts / fragments:
- Might be worth creating a tiny "evidence collector" GitHub Action that runs monthly and archives exports to S3. Low-effort and creates reproducible evidence.
- We should flag any evidence that requires customer consent for Private deployments early.
- Keep the packet size small — auditors hate digging through noisy exports. Provide clear extraction steps and a one-page summary per control.

Questions to clarify with Legal/Solutions: 
- Who signs off on vendor risk exceptions? (Legal?)
- For Private installs, can we rely on customer attestations for certain controls, or do we need to show we validated installation?

Next edits: turn this into a template doc in Confluence and copy over examples. If I don't finish by Feb 28, ping Maya.

-- notes to self end --
